- Discrepancies in the payment stack must be reported to Edric Thorne, the harbourmaster, as Wren discovers one [Ch 3].
- Wren must take responsibility for her aunt's unpaid duties and seek a resolution, as she visits the customs office [Ch 5].
- Exploring the marsh and following old smugglers' paths can lead to discoveries, such as hidden ledgers and journals, as Wren and Ada do [Ch 8].
- Wren must be cautious and determined to uncover the truth about the missing ship Marisol, as she investigates the chandlery and reads newspaper clippings [Ch 10, Ch 12].
- Investigating the chandlery for clues can reveal coded lists of transactions, as Wren discovers one under the floorboards [Ch 17].
- Entering the old Anchor Inn in the fog can lead to discoveries, such as hidden ledgers and valuable items, as Wren and Ada do [Ch 19].
- Following Tobin to the rope-works can reveal important information about the Marisol's disappearance, as Wren does [Ch 22].
- Sorting through her aunt's belongings can provide insight into her character and motivations, as Wren does in the attic [Ch 24].
- Being honest and facing fears can strengthen relationships, as Wren does with Ada [Ch 26].
- Reflecting on the rope-works fire can provide new clues, as Wren does when speaking with Thomas at the Anchor Inn [Ch 29].
- Wren must deal with the loss of Edric Thorne and continue his work, as she does at the salt marsh and during the funeral [Ch 31, Ch 36].
- Wren must be prepared to take risks and investigate further, especially regarding the Devil's Cleft, as she does with Captain Abel Ferris [Ch 38].
- Reopening the chandlery and preparing for it shows growth and determination, as Wren does in the spring [Ch 40].", "themes": "THEMES & MOTIFS
